step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core system actors and services from visual icons and audio transcript: IoT Device (UserConsumerIOT), AWS IoT Core (IoTCore), Elasticsearch/OpenSearch (OpenSearch), CloudWatch (CloudWatch), Lambda (Lambda), SQS (SQS), ECS (ECS), RDS (RDS), ElastiCache (ElastiCache), and Scientists (UserCompanyDomainExpert).
2. Mapped visual arrows and transcript description into logical sequential workflows:
 - Flow 0: Ingestion from IoT Device into AWS IoT Core via TLS/MQTT.
 - Flow 1: IoT Core Rules Engine routing telemetry to Elasticsearch for BI/visualization, and operational logs to CloudWatch for monitoring/alarms.
 - Flow 2: Bidirectional processing loop between IoT Core and Lambda worker.
 - Flow 3: Decoupled workflow sending messages from IoT Core to SQS, processed by ECS backend compute, persisted to RDS (long-term data) and ElastiCache (short-term data), serving the Scientists.

graph.name: Miraculous Genomics IoT Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture for ingesting genomics IoT device data into AWS IoT Core, processing worker workflows via Lambda and ECS, routing metrics/logs to Elasticsearch and CloudWatch, storing long/short term data in RDS and ElastiCache, and serving scientists.

nodes.name: Device
nodes.notes: Genomics IoT device communicating via MQTT over TLS.

nodes.name: IoT Core
nodes.notes: Ingests device data and uses rules engine to route messages.

nodes.name: Elasticsearch
nodes.notes: Stores telemetry and commercial/BI data for querying and visualization.

nodes.name: CloudWatch
nodes.notes: Monitors platform logs and sets alarms.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Worker process that performs computations and returns feedback to IoT Core.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Queues messages to decouple IoT device communication from backend processing.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Backend container compute processing queued messages and serving API.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Relational database used for long-term data storage.

nodes.name: ElastiCache
nodes.notes: In-memory caching layer for quick access to short-term data.

nodes.name: Scientists
nodes.notes: End-user scientists interacting with web application and API.

edges.notes: TLS/MQTT connection from IoT device to AWS IoT Core.
IoT Core Rules Engine routes telemetry data to Elasticsearch for visualization and BI.
IoT Core Rules Engine sends logs and operational metrics to CloudWatch for logging and alarms.
IoT Core invokes Lambda to perform processing as a worker.
Lambda returns processed response back to IoT Core/device.
IoT Core routes user interaction messages to SQS.
ECS polls/consumes messages from SQS to process device data decoupled from ingestion.
ECS persists long-term genomics and API data in RDS.
ECS caches short-term/fast access data in ElastiCache.
Scientists access API and web application backed by ECS compute.
